title: mobframework
brief: "BEAM on device" — write mobile apps in Elixir with the whole BEAM running on the device, rendering native iOS and Android UI; your coding agent attaches to the running app with real state and hot-pushed fixes. Ambitious and unusual.
details: Mob (mobframework.com) — "BEAM on device": Elixir plus the BEAM runtime with native iOS/Android UI, so OTP supervision, GenServers, pattern matching, and the pipe operator run on the phone with the same mental model as the backend. One language, one runtime — no server, no JavaScript, no Swift/Kotlin. Half the point is agent operability: it's plain Erlang distribution, so an AI agent attaches to the live app over the wire and gets real state, real UI, and millisecond feedback — read state (`Mob.Test.assigns`), drive interactions (tap, type, swipe), measure native results (frames, sampled pixels), and hot-load fixes with no rebuild. The harness refuses to lie: `tap_xy` returns an error when nothing actually handled the tap rather than a false success, and coverage gaps are published per platform. Since v0.8 every action gets a "receipt" naming the stages it reached, defects land on a bus as fingerprinted capsules, and post-mortems (BEAM crash dumps, MetricKit, Android exit reasons) can be swept onto the same bus. Includes a two-part agentic coding guide (one agent vs a fleet). Pre-1.0 (v0.9), so the surface still moves.
